Quält euch dieses kleine Wort auch manchmal – „muss“?

„Ich muss das tun“, fühlt sich nach Druck an, nach einer Verpflichtung, nach etwas Schwerem, das die Energie raubt. Aber was passiert, wenn wir dieses eine Wort verändern?

Tomorrow marks 5 months since Jaden left us. I have no idea how I am still able to breathe, still holding on, still managing to get out of bed. But I wasn’t really given a choice. As much as I sometimes just want to stay in the dark abyss of grief, I know Jaden wouldn’t want me to keep suffering. 

Yet the rollercoaster of emotions come and go. It truly does this to you out of nowhere. A song, another person, a mom and her teenage son, a passing memory… anything and everything can be a trigger for the tears to start flowing. 

Some don’t understand and wish I would just “move on” and all that does is make me even more upset because they literally can’t and never will understand unless they go through the same thing. 

It is just not that simple. Sure, some say you have the choice to either stay in this misery or pull yourself out of it and try and make the best of whatever life will throw at you next. And really, that is what I am doing. 

By me diving into the metaphysical world because I want to connect with my child behind the veil isn’t some weird way of me coping. I am not distancing myself from the ones who are still here, it’s simply the only way I am able to deal with the immense pain of his loss. It’s my way and no one has to understand it. 

I have now met so many parents who have lost their children the same way, and it is so heartbreaking to see. It starts as early as 6, 7, 8… it’s unfathomable to say the least. It makes me question so many things. For one, putting a band aid on someone’s mental health with drugs isn’t always the answer. In fact, it can make things so much worse. So in all reality it’s a gamble and that’s the scary part. 

So what are the alternatives? There are so many to list, but here is the issue - it’s often not affordable, and not covered through insurance. Especially because it will be a lifelong therapy. 

I hope one day, things will change and kids will get the help they truly need. Because I am so tired of seeing yet another one of these beautiful souls end their precious life.
